avis.titre: Over a month of use, no results.
avis.texte: Honestly though, I like the feel of these toner pads, they do hydrate the skin but I haven’t seen any benefits of it addressing hyperpigmentation / age spots/ acne spots. Quite a few Korean brands over promise & underdeliver. It’s seems to be the case with Centellian as well (a pity since it’s a decent brand)

I ordered these Medeca Mela Capture Ampoule Pads from Centellian24 because I saw that they had some ferments in them and I'm interested in that. As a matter of fact they contain bifida lysate ferment, the same ferment that is also present in a coveted brand name serum that you all have heard of ;) These pads are meant to brighten and even out the skin tone, soothe and calm, and hydrate / moisturize the skin. And they have the ingredients to do that-- niacinamide and ascorbic acid for brightening, centella, chamomile, beta-glucan and lactobacillus ferment for soothing, and olive oil, triglycerides, centella, and fig extract for moisturizing. When I ran the formulation for these pads through an ingredient decoder program, it came up with 21 "goodies", meaning 21 ingredients that are all working to improve the look and health of the skin. Sadly for me, these pads also contain diphenyl dimethicone which is a silicone. Granted, it is far down on the list, but I don't like to use toners or serums that contain silicones because I worry that the film silicones leave on the skin will interfere with absorption of my moisturizer (the last step in my skincare routine). Despite that concern, I have been using these pads for several days now and like them very much. They smell clean and vaguely citrusy, which does come from added fragrance, another ingredient I could do without. I do think the fragrance is probably there simply to neutralize the smell of other ingredients though (ferments)
